free_tier.stated: 200 GB $3 · 1 TB $5 · 2 TB $8 · 4 TB $10 · 10 TB $25 · 20 TB $42, all per month
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: VERBATIM per-tier transfer caps: 1 TB plan gets "Transfer 2 TB"; 4 TB gets 10 TB; 10 TB gets 15 TB; **20 TB gets only 20 TB of transfer**. So egress is ~1x storage at the top tier, decaying to 0.5x at the 200 GB tier. This is a metered product wearing an 'unlimited hosting' costume.

interface_detail: FTP/FTPS, SFTP, SCP, rsync over non-root SSH, DirectAdmin, Apache/PHP/MySQL, Nextcloud, web file delivery
tooling: Rsync/SFTP. "Object Storage Beta" exists but is beta. Treat as unavailable. No S3, no WebDAV stated.
chaining: DirectAdmin + Apache means you CAN serve HTTP directly from it, which is unusual and useful for a Cloudflare origin. But the 20 TB transfer cap at the 20 TB tier means one full re-sync exhausts the month.
limits_note: No root access on the shared storage product ("Shared storage does not include root access"). Transfer caps are the binding constraint, not capacity.
reliability_note: Long-established (InterServer, since 1999), ZFS + RAID-Z2, 99.9% uptime claim, 24/7 support. Very stable operator. The product is priced to make capacity cheap and bandwidth expensive, which is the opposite of the requirement.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: the full six-tier table with Space and Transfer columns (opened this session)
"Starts at $3.00 per TB per month", "Each storage VPS slice adds 1TB SATA storage, 2GB memory, 2TB transfer" (opened this session)

price_per_tb_month: $2.10/TB/mo at the 20 TB tier ($42) but with only 20 TB/mo of transfer. $2.50/TB/mo at the 10 TB tier with 15 TB transfer. 5 TB workload: buy the 10 TB tier = $2.50/TB/mo. 20 TB workload: $2.10/TB/mo. Cheap per TB, but egress = 1x storage makes it a trap for the 500 GB-1 TiB/day serving load.
